title: Double dualization preserves finite-module injections over a Noetherian domain
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $U,V$ be finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $f:U\to V$ be an injective $R$-linear map. For an $R$-module $W$, write $W^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(W,R)$. Define $f^*:V^*\to U^*$ by $f^*(\varphi)=\varphi\circ f$, and define $f^{**}:U^{**}\to V^{**}$ by $f^{**}(x)(\varphi)=x(\varphi\circ f)$. Then $f^{**}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive), proof of the claim that j is injective, more-algebra.tex:5286-5305. This claim uses only the injectivity of M into M′ and finiteness over the Noetherian domain, not reflexivity of M′ or torsion freeness of M″.

proof.text: Put $S=R\setminus\{0\}$ and $K=S^{-1}R$, the fraction field. Write $P_K=S^{-1}P$ for module localization, with fractions and equality as in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Localizing the exact pair $0\to U\xrightarrow{f}V$ gives an injective $K$-linear map $f_K:U_K\to V_K$, $u/s\mapsto f(u)/s$, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. The ring map $R\to K$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat].

source.place: Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive), proof of the injectivity claim; algebra.tex, Tags 0583, 00CS, 00HT(1), 00DL for the localization inputs.

proof.text: Apply the localization-tensor statement [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with $A=K$, $(M,M',\ell_M)=(K,K,\mathrm{id}_K)$ (the identity of $K$ is a localization at $S$, since every $s\in S$ acts bijectively on $K$) and $(N,N',\ell_N)=(P,P_K,p\mapsto p/1)$: the map $\ell:K\otimes_RP\to K\otimes_KP_K$ is a localization at $S$. Every $s\in S$ already acts bijectively on the $K$-module $K\otimes_RP$, so conditions (b) and (c) make $\ell$ bijective; composing with the unit $K\otimes_KP_K\cong P_K$ identifies $K\otimes_R P$ with $P_K$, for every $R$-module $P$ (we use $P=U,V,U^*,V^*$ and $K\otimes_RR=K$). The resulting maps are $(a/s)\otimes p\mapsto ap/s$ and $p/s\mapsto (1/s)\otimes p$. The tensor unit maps are $r\otimes p\mapsto rp$ and $a\otimes z\mapsto az$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented], including its Noetherian finite-module clause, to $(M,N)=(U,R)$ and $(V,R)$. It gives bijections $\theta_P:S^{-1}P^*\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(P_K,K)$ for $P=U,V$, with $\theta_P(\varphi/s)(p/t)=\varphi(p)/(st)$. No finite presentation of the dual modules is needed. On $u/t$, both $\theta_U((\psi\circ f)/s)$ and $\theta_V(\psi/s)\circ f_K$ equal $\psi(f(u))/(st)$; thus these bijections intertwine restriction along $f$ and $f_K$.

source.place: Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive), proof of the injectivity claim; algebra.tex, Tags 0583, 00CS, 00HT(1), 00DL for the localization inputs.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement], choose $V_K=f_K(U_K)\oplus C$. For any $\alpha:U_K\to K$, define $\beta:V_K\to K$ by $\beta(f_K(u)+c)=\alpha(u)$ for $u\in U_K$, $c\in C$. Unique decomposition and injectivity of $f_K$ make this well-defined. Addition and scalar multiplication of decompositions show it is $K$-linear, and $\beta f_K=\alpha$. Consequently restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_K(V_K,K)\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(U_K,K)$ is surjective.

e0$ with $t(\psi\circ f-s\varphi)=0$. Hence $(t\psi)\circ f=(ts)\varphi$, with $ts

source.place: Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive), proof of the injectivity claim; algebra.tex, Tags 0583, 00CS, 00HT(1), 00DL for the localization inputs.

proof.text: Let $x\in U^{**}$ satisfy $f^{**}(x)=0$. For $\varphi\in U^*$ choose $s,t,\psi$ as in Step 4. By $R$-linearity and the defining formula for $f^{**}$, $ts\,x(\varphi)=x(ts\varphi)=x((t\psi)\circ f)=f^{**}(x)(t\psi)=0$. Since $ts\ne0$ in the integral domain $R$, $x(\varphi)=0$. This holds for every $\varphi$, so $x=0$. Finally, if $f^{**}(x)=f^{**}(y)$, linearity gives $f^{**}(x-y)=0$, whence $x=y$.
